method: Actual macOS application-window captures during UI actions. Pauses between steps removed. Source frame timing retained within steps; final frames held when needed for caption reading. No generated UI animation. Not a latency measurement.

videos.title: Expressive playing with independent virtual fingers

steps.caption: Mouse: press, drag horizontally and release. Firmware interprets the continuous contact.
Enable Latch new fingers. Press A, F and K to hold three separated contacts.
Select finger 131 (A). Press Right six times: only this finger moves in X.
Select finger 132 (F). Press Up four times: only this finger moves in Y.
Select finger 133 (K). Press [ ten times to reduce only its pressure.
Open the inspector view: separate contact X/Y/Z values and raw firmware MIDI are visible.
Release all removes all three fingers and sends their releases. Turn Latch off.
Choose Chord pads. Default harmony: C major, triads, root position.
Enable Latch new fingers. Click bottom-row pad 1: hold degree I (C major).
Host shows the resulting chord: MIDI 60, 64, 67. One finger holds three output notes.
Release I, then click bottom-row pad 6 for VI (A minor).
Degree VI produces MIDI 69, 72, 76. Release before the next chord.
Release VI; click bottom-row pad 4 for IV (F major).
Degree IV produces MIDI 65, 69, 72.
Release IV; click bottom-row pad 5 for V (G major).
Degree V produces MIDI 67, 71, 74. This completes I–VI–IV–V.
Release the finger. Set Inversion to 1, then Apply harmony.
Click pad I again. The same C chord now uses first inversion.
First inversion: MIDI 64, 67, 72. Held chord identity remains C.
Release the finger and return Inversion to 0.
Choose Chord: Seventh, then Apply harmony.
Click pad I to play C major seventh.
Seventh adds B: MIDI 60, 64, 67, 71. All four voices belong to one held finger.
Release all. Restore Triad for the next exercise.
Choose Strum low to high. Set Step spacing to 1/2 beat; Apply harmony.
Start Record selected. The following held finger will record the staggered chord attacks.
Click and latch pad I. The three chord tones attack in ascending order, 1/2 beat apart.
Release all; Finish take. Scroll to the note editor to inspect the staggered attacks.
Choose Arpeggio low to high: 1/2-beat steps, 1/4-beat gate. Apply harmony.
Latch pad I. One held finger starts a repeating C–E–G arpeggio.
Watch the capture: repeated note attacks and releases continue while the finger is held.
Release all cancels future arpeggio attacks. No finger remains held.
Choose Humanized chord. Delay 60000 ticks, velocity variation ±8, seed 42; Apply harmony.
Latch pad I. Humanized chord applies bounded attack delay and velocity variation.
Inspect output timestamps and velocities: the same C triad has varied attacks.
Release all. Restore Together articulation for manual picking.
Set Playing to Strumplate. Select degree I and Apply harmony.
Enable Latch. Click five separate bottom-row pads to pick C–E–G–C–E across octaves.
Five independent pad attacks produce five held chord tones. Release all ends the picked notes.
Select degree VI. The same pad positions now pick tones of A minor.
Click the first three bottom-row pads: A, C and E. Release all afterward.
Prepare a custom chord: Release all, choose Play mode, then select degree I.
In Play mode, latch keys A, F and K to hold three ordinary notes.
Click Learn held notes to selected degree. Degree I now stores MIDI 42, 45, 49.
Release fingers; choose Chord pads as the Playing style, Apply harmony, then Chord pads mode.
Click pad I: one finger now recalls the three learned pitches.
The host confirms the learned voicing. Its stored pitches replace the diatonic triad.
Release all; restore the selected degree to diatonic harmony.

videos.title: Record, loop and launch an expressive phrase

steps.caption: Choose empty slot 02. Click Record selected in Play mode.
Open the instrument and click Play scripted phrase: three contacts move independently through firmware.
Return to the host and click Finish take. Slot 02 now contains the expressive phrase.
Inspect the recorded notes. Their original timing and expression are retained.
Choose Clip pads mode, then open the firmware surface.
Click bottom-row pad 2. Blue recorded state changes to green while clip 02 plays.
Host confirms slot 02 PLAYING. Scheduled MIDI includes recorded per-note expression.
Return to Play mode without stopping the clip. Latch A to play a live note beside playback.
Observe live and clip output in the capture sink. Each voice keeps its own expression.
Release the live finger. Stop all ends clip playback.
With recorded slot 02 selected, click Overdub. Existing notes are kept.
Play another scripted phrase through the firmware while overdub is active.
Finish take commits the added notes. The editor now shows both layers.
Click Undo to remove the overdub and restore the previous phrase.
For retrospective capture, select empty slot 03. Set tempo to 60 BPM; four beats now span four seconds.
Without recording, play the scripted phrase. Immediately click Capture last 4 beats in the host.
Slot 03 contains the recent performance. Inspect the recovered notes.
Click the selected slot 03 to loop the recovered phrase. Stop selected ends playback.
Stop selected. Restore 120 BPM before the accompaniment exercise.

videos.title: Euclidean accompaniment, harmony following and freeze

steps.caption: Select stopped slot 04. Set live harmony to degree I in C major.
Open Accompaniment. Use 16 steps, 5 pulses, tone range -3 to -3 and Follow active harmony.
Generate selected slot. Five root notes form a four-beat bass pattern; launch slot 04.
Choose Clip pads. Enable Latch, then press top-row pad 6 to select VI (A minor).
Host confirms VI is the follower harmony. The running bass now uses A below the chord.
Click IV in the host. Future bass attacks follow F while the five-pulse rhythm stays unchanged.
Click V. Future bass attacks follow G; already sounding notes retain their pitches.
Stop selected. Open Accompaniment and click Freeze current harmony to store G bass pitches.
Select I in Harmony after freezing. Relaunch slot 04; its bass no longer follows chord changes.
Capture confirms repeated MIDI 55 (hex 37): the frozen G bass persists under selected harmony I.
Stop selected and select stopped slot 05. Open Accompaniment for a separate seeded melody.
Set tone range 0 to 5, Seed 42, and turn following off. Generate selected slot.
Launch slot 05. The saved pitch pattern replays without drawing a new take on each loop.
Stop selected and release the harmony-selection finger. The generated clips remain saved in memory.

videos.title: Multiple clips, quantized launch and temporary controls

steps.caption: Set Launch grid to 4 beats. Launch recorded slots 04 and 05 from the surface.
Two green bottom-row pads show the running bass and melody clips. Enable Latch for a sustained hold.
Click row 1, column 5: hold mute for melody clip 05. Its pad turns cyan while the loop continues.
Release all removes the mute hold. The melody pad returns green and future attacks resume.
Click row 4, column 5: hold octave up for clip 05. Magenta shows the temporary shift.
Release all restores original future pitches. Stored notes are unchanged.
Turn Latch off. Stop all in the host; running clips return to recorded state.
The firmware surface shows blue recorded pads after playback stops.

videos.title: Periodic note conditions and held Fill

steps.caption: Select empty slot 06. Generate a one-beat test clip: 4 steps, 1 pulse, tone range 0 to 0.
Select the note with Next note. Choose Loop N of period, Loop N 4, Period 4; Apply note condition.
Launch slot 06. One attack occurs on loops 4, 8, 12…; other loops skip the note.
Stop selected. Change Playback condition to While Fill held, then Apply note condition.
Launch slot 06 again. With Fill released, no new note attacks are emitted.
Enable Latch and click row 6, column 1: hold Fill. The pad changes from yellow to magenta.
While Fill is held, the note plays every loop. The capture stream now advances on every beat.
Release all clears Fill. Future attacks stop, while the clip keeps looping.
Stop selected completes the exercise.

videos.title: Per-note locks and A/B morph — capture only

steps.caption: Stop slot 06 and restore Every loop. Apply a note parameter: reference 0, value 32768.
Launch slot 06. Open A/B MORPH to inspect voice-scoped parameter events from each attack.
Each captured attack carries parameter 0 = 32768 on its own voice. No audible mapping is connected.
Stop selected. Click Add parameter to configure an A/B morph endpoint.
Parameter 1 maps State A = 0 to State B = 65535. Add a second parameter for an inverse curve.
Set parameter 2 to A = 65535, B = 0. Apply A/B endpoints.
Click State A, then State B. The capture shows opposite endpoint values for parameters 1 and 2.
Latch a finger on row 2 (third row from bottom). Press Right twenty times to move the contact in small steps.
The capture now lists successive global values: parameter 1 rises while parameter 2 falls.
Release all. The last morph value remains; releasing a finger does not reset parameters.

videos.title: Edit, quantize, duplicate and save a session

steps.caption: Select recorded slot 03. Collapse A/B MORPH and select a recovered note with Next note.
Change Note to 65, Start ticks to 1200000 and Duration ticks to 480000. Apply edit.
Undo restores the original pitch and timing. Expression stays attached to the edited note.
Choose Attack grid: 1/4 beat. Quantize clip attacks aligns note starts explicitly.
Undo restores free timing. Select slot 06 and Duplicate to next to copy it into empty slot 07.
Set Session file path to /tmp/crest-manual-video-session.json and click Save session.
Click Reopen. Saved clips, output profiles and parameter endpoints return; playback remains stopped.
